actions.action: Inspect plants, especially leaf undersides, for thrips damage, frass and insects
Isolate the affected plant and any nearby plants
Spray spinosad (e.g. Captain Jack's) outdoors out of direct sun, weekly until no new signs, treating all plants
Apply a systemic insecticide to the soil (e.g. Bonide granules), repeating every 6-8 weeks
Alternative: hang predatory mite sachets on the plants
Canada alternative: alternate pyrethrin spray with insecticidal soap weekly
After 2 healthy new leaves grow, remove the worst-damaged old leaf and repeat

verdict.reason: The answer correctly identifies thrips as the main problem (missing low light) and recommends spinosad plus systemic treatment matching the successful fix, with no harmful advice.
